rounds.critic: Independent visual critic, corrective Saurian Future Farm role comparison
rounds.inspection: Reviewed the archived painted Farm and Hydroponics Tower age cells and both unpainted Farm views from the held canonical pages. The previous GLB had already been replaced. Its evidence hash, triangle counts and technical score come from the prior matching review.

models.observations: Both painted age cells show a small mound of leaf-crowned circular trays in the middle of a largely bare brown plot. The same vertically tiered form dominates both neutral views. The Hydroponics Tower next to it has a taller stack but the same arrangement of planted rims around a central axis. At phone scale the difference is height, and there is too little ground cultivation to identify the Farm. The earlier serialized technical score and triangle counts are carried forward from the matching prior record.
defects: Move production onto the ground plane. Expose sizable planted rows, water distribution or agricultural access around a smaller service structure so the building reads as a farm beside the Hydroponics Tower in both neutral phone views.

rounds.critic: Independent visual critic, revised Saurian Future Farm
rounds.inspection: Opened both age previews and rendered the three serialized LODs at 64 px. Compared two neutral 64 px views against every Farm era, Hydroponics Tower and both Industrial Farm eras, then inspected LOD0 and LOD1 in colour at 218 px from four angles. Verified fragment, triangle ratios, geometry and shell orientation at the new evidence hash.

models.observations: Four curved planting beds span the open blue irrigation deck. Repeated leafy crops trace the field rows from either direction, and a small corner shelter gives them a scale. In two unpainted 64 px views this low horizontal plan separates from the Hydroponics Tower’s vertical stack, the Industrial Farm’s greenhouse roofs and silos, and the older Farm’s terraces and machinery. Painted LOD1 retains the crop rows, planter walls, shelter roof and clear access around them when viewed from either side or behind. LOD2 keeps the parallel bands. Information and Ascension share a restrained blue-green palette, with the pier and trim providing the subtler age change. Serialized metadata and LOD ratios passed, with zero exposed coplanar pairs or inverted closed shells.

models.observations: A thatched hunting lookout on tall timber stilts rises beside a drying rack. A ladder reaches the platform and a small turquoise jar stands below. Its open framework separates it from the earlier closed hut in both grey angles. Painted previews cover classical, medieval. I compared both 64 px unpainted family views and the 215°, 125° and 35° painted middle LOD. Serialized LODs 821/467/241 passed validation and the 60% ceiling. Direct surface and winding checks found zero exposed coplanar overlaps and zero inverted closed shells. The largest directed corner share involving this model and any sibling was 0.0%.
